newsitem.title: UK: BT cuts prices of high-speed digital service.
newsitem.headline: BT cuts prices of high-speed digital service.

text.p: British Telecommunications said on Thursday it had cut some of the prices of its high-speed digital ISDN2 (Integrated Services Digital Network) services after the industry regulator complained they were not competitive enough.

Telecom regulator Oftel welcomed the changes, which cut the rental charge of BT's "low start" pricing option by almost 100 stg to 352 stg and the connections charge of its "fast start" option to 500 stg from 680 stg.
However, some prices, such as its "start up" connection charge at 199 stg, remain unchanged. "Fast start" and "start up" rental charges rise by 15 stg each -- both to 535 stg.

The Integrated Services Digital Network services are the first step on the road to the information superhighway for many small businesses, schools and some individuals, and for many of these, the service is primarily available through BT's ISDN2.
Oftel director general Don Cruickshank said he was pleased that BT was trying to meet his concerns about tariffs.
"The changes BT is now making address the anti-competitive effects which I identified, and include some worthwhile price cuts," he said in a statement.
